title: Ecclesiastes Chapter 8 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Ecclesiastes chapter 8 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Ecclesiastes Chapter 8 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Ecclesiastes Chapter 8.

questions.question: Who is compared to the wise man in Ecclesiastes 8:1?
questions.explanation: The verse asks, 'Who is as the wise man?' implying there is no equal to a wise man.

questions.question: What does a man's wisdom do to his face according to Ecclesiastes 8:1?
questions.explanation: The verse states that 'a man's wisdom maketh his face to shine.'

questions.question: What should one counsel according to Ecclesiastes 8:2?
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 8:2 advises to 'keep the king's commandment.'

questions.question: According to Ecclesiastes 8:3, what should one not be hasty to do?
questions.explanation: The verse advises 'Be not hasty to go out of his sight.'

questions.question: Where does power exist according to Ecclesiastes 8:4?
options: In the word of a king
In the hearts of the people
questions.correctAnswer: In the word of a king
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 8:4 states, 'Where the word of a king is, there is power.'

questions.question: True or False: Ecclesiastes 8:5 states that whoso keepeth the commandment shall feel no evil thing.
questions.explanation: The verse clearly states, 'Whoso keepeth the commandment shall feel no evil thing.'

questions.question: True or False: A wise man's heart cannot discern time and judgment according to Ecclesiastes 8:5.
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 8:5 indicates that 'a wise man's heart discerneth both time and judgment.'

questions.question: What does Ecclesiastes 8:6 say about time and judgment?
options: There is a time for every purpose
They are only for the wicked
questions.correctAnswer: There is a time for every purpose
questions.explanation: The verse declares, 'Because to every purpose there is time and judgment.'

questions.question: True or False: Ecclesiastes 8:7 says that man knows what shall be.
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 8:7 states, 'For he knoweth not that which shall be.'

questions.question: What does Ecclesiastes 8:9 mention about man's rule over another?
options: It is done for the good of all
It can lead to his own hurt
questions.correctAnswer: It can lead to his own hurt
questions.explanation: The verse notes, 'there is a time wherein one man ruleth over another to his own hurt.'

questions.question: In Ecclesiastes 8:10, what is said about the wicked after they are buried?
questions.explanation: The verse mentions, 'they were forgotten in the city where they had so done.'

questions.question: True or False: Ecclesiastes 8:14 claims that just men may suffer as the wicked.
questions.explanation: The verse states, 'that there be just men, unto whom it happeneth according to the work of the wicked.'

questions.question: In Ecclesiastes 8, which instruction comes before all the others listed here?
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 8:2 provides the first instruction to 'keep the king's commandment.'

questions.question: What is commended in Ecclesiastes 8:15?
questions.explanation: The verse states, 'Then I commended mirth.'

medium.title: Ecclesiastes Chapter 8 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Ecclesiastes Chapter 8 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What is said about a wise man's heart in response to keeping the commandments?
options: It discerns both time and judgment
questions.correctAnswer: It discerns both time and judgment
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 8:5 highlights that a wise man's heart discerns both time and judgment, indicating that wisdom provides insight into when to act and how to respond to life's circumstances.

questions.question: According to Ecclesiastes 8:8, what power does man lack?
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 8:8 states that no man has power over the spirit to retain it, which signifies the ultimate lack of control over life and death.

questions.question: True or False: The heart of the sons of men is fully set to do good because evil works are not punished quickly.
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 8:11 indicates that because sentence against an evil work is not executed speedily, the heart of the sons of men is fully set in them to do evil, not good.

questions.question: What happens to those who fear God according to Ecclesiastes 8:12?
options: It shall be well with them
questions.correctAnswer: It shall be well with them
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 8:12 assures that it will be well with those who fear God, indicating that reverence for God leads to a favorable outcome.

questions.question: How does Ecclesiastes 8:10 illustrate the fate of the wicked?
options: They will be buried and forgotten
questions.correctAnswer: They will be buried and forgotten
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 8:10 notes that the wicked are buried and forgotten, highlighting the transient nature of their existence and the vanity associated with it.

questions.question: True or False: Ecclesiastes 8:7 suggests that man can predict the future.
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 8:7 states that man does not know what shall be, emphasizing the uncertainty of the future and our lack of ability to predict it.

questions.question: What does Ecclesiastes 8:14 reveal about the fate of just and wicked men?
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 8:14 describes a vanity where just men suffer as the wicked and wicked men fare as the just, illustrating the perplexities of life.

questions.question: According to Ecclesiastes 8:1, what effect does a man's wisdom have on his face?
options: It makes his face to shine
questions.correctAnswer: It makes his face to shine
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 8:1 states that a man's wisdom makes his face to shine, indicating that wisdom brings clarity and positivity.

questions.question: What is the advice given in Ecclesiastes 8:2 regarding the king's commandment?
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 8:2 advises to keep the king's commandment, emphasizing the importance of obedience to authority as a principle of wisdom.

questions.question: How does Ecclesiastes 8:6 relate to understanding human misery?
options: Every purpose has time and judgment
questions.correctAnswer: Every purpose has time and judgment
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 8:6 highlights that every purpose has a time and judgment, suggesting that understanding this helps alleviate the experience of human misery.

questions.question: True or False: Ecclesiastes 8:3 encourages haste in leaving the king's presence.
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 8:3 advises not to be hasty to go out of the king's sight, indicating that one should be careful and deliberate in such situations.

questions.question: What does Ecclesiastes 8:16 suggest about the pursuit of wisdom?
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 8:16 mentions that applying one's heart to know wisdom and observe the work done upon the earth can lead to sleeplessness, indicating the exhaustive nature of such a pursuit.

questions.question: What conclusion does the author of Ecclesiastes reach about human efforts in understanding God's work?
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 8:17 concludes that despite a man's labor to seek out the work of God, he shall not find it, emphasizing the mystery surrounding divine actions.

hard.title: Ecclesiastes Chapter 8 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Ecclesiastes Chapter 8.

questions.question: According to Ecclesiastes 8:13, what happens to the wicked in relation to their days?
options: It shall not be well with them
questions.correctAnswer: It shall not be well with them
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 8:13 states that 'it shall not be well with the wicked, neither shall he prolong his days, which are as a shadow; because he feareth not before God.' This emphasizes the fate of the wicked due to their lack of reverence for God.

questions.question: What does Ecclesiastes 8:14 say about the fate of just and wicked men?
options: Just men prosper while wicked men suffer
Wicked men prosper while just men suffer
Both just and wicked men face vanity
questions.correctAnswer: Both just and wicked men face vanity
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 8:14 describes a vanity on earth where just men face outcomes similar to wicked men, indicating the perplexity of life where justice is not always apparent.

questions.question: What does the phrase 'there is a time and judgment' refer to in Ecclesiastes 8:6?
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 8:6 states that 'Because to every purpose there is time and judgment, therefore the misery of man is great upon him.' This indicates that man struggles with understanding timing and judgment.

questions.question: According to Ecclesiastes 8:15, what is considered the best thing a man can do under the sun?
options: To eat, drink, and be merry
questions.correctAnswer: To eat, drink, and be merry
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 8:15 states, 'Then I commended mirth, because a man hath no better thing under the sun, than to eat, and to drink, and to be merry.' This reflects the joy found in simple pleasures amidst life's uncertainties.

questions.question: What literary device is present in Ecclesiastes 8:14 regarding the fate of just and wicked men?
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 8:14 uses parallelism by contrasting the fates of just men and wicked men, illustrating the theme of vanity in their outcomes. This device emphasizes the complexity of justice.

questions.question: Which other Biblical passage emphasizes the idea that the wicked will not escape judgment, similar to Ecclesiastes 8:13?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 11:21 states, 'Though hand join in hand, the wicked shall not be unpunished: but the seed of the righteous shall be delivered.' This aligns with Ecclesiastes 8:13 regarding the fate of the wicked.

questions.question: What does Ecclesiastes 8:8 say about man's power over the spirit?
options: No man has power over the spirit
questions.correctAnswer: No man has power over the spirit
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 8:8 states, 'There is no man that hath power over the spirit to retain the spirit; neither hath he power in the day of death.' This reflects the ultimate sovereignty of God over life and death.

questions.question: True or False: Ecclesiastes 8:12 asserts that it is well with those who fear God.
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 8:12 states, 'Though a sinner do evil an hundred times, and his days be prolonged, yet surely I know that it shall be well with them that fear God.' This confirms that those who fear God will fare better.

questions.question: What does Ecclesiastes 8:7 suggest about man's knowledge of the future?
options: Man knows not what shall be
Man has full control over his fate
questions.correctAnswer: Man knows not what shall be
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 8:7 states, 'For he knoweth not that which shall be: for who can tell him when it shall be?' This highlights the uncertainty of human foresight.

questions.question: According to Ecclesiastes 8:10, what happened to the wicked who were buried?
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 8:10 indicates that the wicked were forgotten in the city where they had done their deeds, illustrating the fleeting nature of their legacy.

questions.question: True or False: Ecclesiastes 8:9 indicates that one man can rule over another without consequences.
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 8:9 states, 'there is a time wherein one man ruleth over another to his own hurt,' indicating that such rule can lead to negative outcomes.

questions.question: What key Hebrew word in Ecclesiastes 8:15 refers to joy or merriment?
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word 'Simcha' relates to joy or merriment, as seen in Ecclesiastes 8:15 where mirth is commended.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the theme of enjoying life in the present, similar to Ecclesiastes 8:15?
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 10:31 states, 'Whether therefore ye eat, or drink, or whatsoever ye do, do all to the glory of God.' This aligns with the theme of enjoying life’s gifts as presented in Ecclesiastes 8:15.

questions.question: In Ecclesiastes 8:16, what does the author apply his heart to know?
options: Wisdom and the business done on earth
questions.correctAnswer: Wisdom and the business done on earth
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 8:16 states, 'When I applied mine heart to know wisdom, and to see the business that is done upon the earth.' This shows the author's pursuit of understanding.

questions.question: What conclusion does the author reach about man's ability to understand God's work in Ecclesiastes 8:17?
options: Man can fully understand God's work
God's work is easy to comprehend
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 8:17 states, 'that a man cannot find out the work that is done under the sun: because though a man labour to seek it out, yet he shall not find it.' This emphasizes the limitations of human understanding.

theological.title: Ecclesiastes Chapter 8 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Ecclesiastes Chapter 8 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What does Ecclesiastes 8:1 suggest about a wise man's appearance?
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 8:1 states that a man's wisdom maketh his face to shine, indicating that wisdom is reflected in one's demeanor.

questions.question: According to Ecclesiastes 8:2, what should one keep in regard to the king?
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 8:2 advises to keep the king's commandment, showing the importance of obedience to authority.

questions.question: What does Ecclesiastes 8:5 say about those who keep the commandment?
options: They will feel no evil thing
They will be feared by others
questions.correctAnswer: They will feel no evil thing
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 8:5 states that whoso keepeth the commandment shall feel no evil thing, indicating protection in obedience.

questions.question: What does Ecclesiastes 8:7 express about man's knowledge of future events?
options: Man knows when he will die
Man does not know what will be
questions.correctAnswer: Man does not know what will be
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 8:7 emphasizes that for he knoweth not that which shall be, highlighting human ignorance of future matters.

questions.question: According to Ecclesiastes 8:10, what happens to the wicked after their death?
options: They are forgotten in the city
questions.correctAnswer: They are forgotten in the city
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 8:10 notes that the wicked are forgotten in the city where they had lived, indicating the fleeting nature of their legacy.

questions.question: What does Ecclesiastes 8:13 reveal about the fate of the wicked?
options: They will not prolong their days
questions.correctAnswer: They will not prolong their days
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 8:13 states that it shall not be well with the wicked, indicating that their days are not extended.

questions.question: What does Ecclesiastes 8:14 suggest about the apparent injustice in life?
options: It is a test of faith
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 8:14 states that this is also vanity, expressing the perplexing nature of justice in life.

questions.question: Which attribute of God is suggested by the power of the king in Ecclesiastes 8:4?
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 8:4 emphasizes the power of the king, reflecting God's sovereignty over all earthly authority.

questions.question: What two themes are combined in Ecclesiastes 8:5 and Ecclesiastes 8:6 regarding the wise man's discernment?
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 8:5 and 8:6 together highlight that a wise man's heart discerneth both time and judgment, underscoring the importance of discernment.

questions.question: What does Ecclesiastes 8:16 suggest about the nature of human understanding?
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 8:16 indicates that a man cannot find out the work that is done under the sun, illustrating the limits of human understanding.

questions.question: Skeptics claim that human efforts to understand life are futile. What does Ecclesiastes 8:17 actually teach?
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 8:17 teaches that though a wise man think to know it, yet shall he not be able to find it, affirming the limits of human comprehension.

questions.question: What is the primary encouragement given in Ecclesiastes 8:15 regarding life under the sun?
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 8:15 states that a man hath no better thing under the sun, than to eat, drink, and be merry, encouraging enjoyment of life's simple pleasures.

questions.question: What does Ecclesiastes 8:12 imply about the relationship between sin and the fear of God?
options: Fear of God leads to punishment
It shall be well with those who fear God
questions.correctAnswer: It shall be well with those who fear God
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 8:12 implies that those who fear God will have a better outcome than sinners who act without regard to divine authority.

questions.question: How does Ecclesiastes 8:9 reflect on the nature of authority?
options: It can lead to personal harm
questions.correctAnswer: It can lead to personal harm
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 8:9 reflects that there is a time wherein one man ruleth over another to his own hurt, indicating the potential pitfalls of authority.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is suggested by the inability of man to control the spirit as stated in Ecclesiastes 8:8?
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 8:8 indicates that there is no man that hath power over the spirit, suggesting God's transcendence over human existence.
